coverage_note: Core vanilla mission files for Chernarus, Livonia and Sakhal are explained here. Always compare with the active vanilla library for the selected map and version; PC mod files need the exact mod author's schema.

files.name: types.xml
files.purpose: Defines Central Economy item targets, cleanup lifetime, restock timing, quantity ranges, counting flags and eligible loot categories, usages and tiers.
files.relationship: An item can be plentiful in types.xml and still not spawn in a building when its category, usage or tier does not match an eligible loot point.
files.restart: Restart required for the server to load economy changes.
files.warning: Never replace the complete live file with a small snippet. Merge complete <type> records and keep every unrelated entry.

files.name: cfgspawnabletypes.xml
files.purpose: Controls attachments, cargo, nested cargo, presets and spawn damage for supported entities such as weapons, bags, infected and vehicles.
files.relationship: The <type name> and every item classname must exist for the active DayZ build. It changes what an entity carries; it does not set that entity's total world population.
files.warning: Chance is normally 0 to 1. Exact vehicle fuel-tank and radiator levels are not configured here; fuel and water can instead be supplied as cargo.

files.name: cfgrandompresets.xml
files.purpose: Defines reusable cargo and attachment preset lists with probabilities.
files.relationship: A preset name referenced by cfgspawnabletypes.xml must match a preset defined here exactly.
files.warning: Check that all classnames and probability values are valid for the selected map and game version.

files.name: cfglimitsdefinition.xml
files.purpose: Defines the allowed category, tag, usage and value names used by the Central Economy.
files.relationship: A custom category, usage or tier/value cannot safely be referenced elsewhere until it is defined in the matching limits definitions.
files.warning: Prefer the user definitions file for supported custom definitions so vanilla definitions remain easy to compare after an update.

files.name: economy.xml
files.purpose: Controls whether broad economy groups such as dynamic items, animals, infected, vehicles, custom objects, buildings and players are initialized, loaded, respawned and saved.
files.relationship: Its init, load, respawn and save switches affect whole economy groups, not individual item quantities.
files.restart: Restart required; persistence changes can have wide effects.
files.warning: Do not change these global switches as a shortcut for a single item or event.

files.name: globals.xml
files.purpose: Stores global Central Economy values such as cleanup distances, respawn behaviour and default loot damage ranges.
files.relationship: A specific cfgspawnabletypes.xml damage rule can override the global loot-damage behaviour for that entity.
files.warning: One global value can affect the whole server; preserve every unrelated variable.

files.name: events.xml
files.purpose: Defines event population, lifetime, radii, position mode, limit mode and child classnames for vehicles, infected, animals, loot and dynamic/static scenes.
files.relationship: For a fixed custom event, the event name must match cfgeventspawns.xml exactly. Child classnames must exist. A grouped scene also needs the matching group definition.
files.warning: Not every event needs four files: cfgeventgroups.xml is only needed for grouped layouts, and mapgroupproto.xml is only needed when the spawned object requires an appropriate loot prototype.

files.name: cfgeventspawns.xml
files.purpose: Provides world positions and headings for named Central Economy events.
files.relationship: Its event name must match events.xml. A position using a group attribute must match a group in cfgeventgroups.xml.
files.warning: X and Z are horizontal world coordinates; A is heading. Y is used only by structures that support or require an explicit height.

files.name: cfgeventgroups.xml
files.purpose: Defines multi-object event layouts as child objects positioned relative to a group origin.
files.relationship: The group name used by an event spawn position must match a <group name> here exactly. Child offsets and angles are relative to the selected group origin.
files.warning: Use this only for a grouped scene. A simple single-child fixed event normally does not need a new group.

files.name: cfgplayerspawnpoints.xml
files.purpose: Controls fresh-player spawn locations and the map-specific spawn selection structure.
files.relationship: This chooses where a fresh character appears; spawn gear is configured separately through a referenced spawn-gear JSON file.
files.warning: Use the correct vanilla structure for the selected map. Do not paste a spawn-points file from another map.

files.name: env/*_territories.xml
files.purpose: Defines dynamic and static zones for infected and animal populations, including position, radius and minimum/maximum counts.
files.relationship: Zone names and event families must be valid for the selected animal or infected territory file. Territory zones are different from fixed CE event positions.
files.warning: Very large dmin/dmax values or overlapping zones can damage server performance.

files.name: cfggameplay.json
files.purpose: Controls supported gameplay settings and provides file lists for object spawners, spawn gear and restricted areas.
files.relationship: enableCfgGameplayFile must be enabled in serverDZ.cfg. Every referenced relative path must match the uploaded filename and folder exactly.
files.warning: Preserve the selected map's complete JSON structure. JSON does not allow comments or trailing commas.

files.name: custom/*.json
files.purpose: Holds custom object placements, spawn-gear presets and other supported custom JSON data.
files.relationship: The custom file does nothing until the correct cfggameplay.json array references its exact relative path.
files.restart: Restart required for mission data changes.
files.warning: Different JSON features use different schemas. An ObjectSpawner file is not interchangeable with spawn gear or a restricted-area file.

files.name: cfgweather.xml
files.purpose: Controls file-based overcast, fog, rain, wind and storm behaviour when the mission uses this weather system.
files.relationship: Check whether init.c or a world script already controls weather before enabling a second weather system.
files.warning: Rain thresholds depend on overcast limits. Valid XML alone does not guarantee the requested weather pattern is logically reachable.

files.name: cfgEffectArea.json
files.purpose: Defines supported static effect or contaminated areas and their positions, shapes and effects.
files.relationship: Static configured areas use this file; dynamic contaminated-area events are controlled by the Central Economy event chain.
files.warning: Do not mix dynamic-event snippets into this JSON schema.

files.name: cfgundergroundtriggers.json
files.purpose: Defines outer, transitional and inner underground triggers plus breadcrumbs that control eye accommodation and underground ambience.
files.relationship: Trigger volumes and breadcrumb positions must form a coherent transition through the actual underground space.
files.warning: This is map geometry-specific. Copying vanilla trigger coordinates to another map will not create a valid underground area.

files.name: mapgroupproto.xml
files.purpose: Describes supported building/group prototypes, loot containers and loot points inside those objects.
files.relationship: mapgrouppos.xml places a named group; mapgroupproto.xml describes where loot can appear inside that group. Loot categories/usages must agree with eligible types.xml entries.
files.warning: Do not paste map placement records into this prototype file. Its root and record structure are different.

files.name: mapgrouppos.xml
files.purpose: Places named map groups/buildings at world coordinates and orientations.
files.relationship: A placed group name needs a matching supported prototype when it is expected to provide Central Economy loot points.
files.warning: This is placement data, not an ObjectSpawner JSON file and not a list of internal loot points.

files.name: messages.xml
files.purpose: Configures supported scheduled in-game server messages, timing and repetition.
files.relationship: Messages are independent of Discord announcements. The supported file can be created when a map package does not ship one, provided the server version supports it.
files.warning: Keep timing values valid and avoid flooding players with overlapping repeating messages.

files.name: serverDZ.cfg
files.purpose: Controls core server settings and enables supported features such as cfggameplay.json.
files.relationship: A valid cfggameplay.json is ignored when enableCfgGameplayFile is not enabled here.
files.warning: Console hosting panels may expose only supported settings rather than direct file access.

files.name: init.c
files.purpose: Mission initialization script used for supported scripted setup, custom hive initialization and weather behaviour.
files.relationship: Scripted weather or spawning can conflict with file-driven systems that attempt to control the same feature.
files.warning: Console and PC capabilities differ. Mod-specific code requires the exact mod and server environment; never assume a PC script works on console.

files.name: cfgeconomycore.xml
files.purpose: Defines Central Economy root classes, defaults and diagnostic logging switches.
files.relationship: Its root classes tell the economy which class families are managed; logging defaults can help diagnose CE behaviour in server reports.
files.warning: This is an advanced economy file. Do not add individual loot entries here.

terms.meaning: The Central Economy target population for that type or event.
terms.rule: For types.xml, keep nominal greater than or equal to min.

terms.meaning: The lower threshold that causes the economy to begin refilling toward nominal.
terms.rule: It is not always the number that appears instantly after a restart.

terms.meaning: The maximum event/child population or potential spawn count in the context where it appears.
terms.rule: Read it together with nominal, min and the event limit mode.

terms.meaning: Seconds an untouched item or event object can remain before cleanup.
terms.rule: Player interaction and persistence can affect when cleanup actually occurs.

terms.meaning: Seconds used by the economy when adding population back toward nominal; zero commonly allows bulk refill behaviour.
terms.rule: It is not the lifetime and does not force an invalid spawn location.

terms.meaning: Minimum and maximum percentage quantity for quantity-bearing items such as magazines, food, liquids or stacked items.
terms.rule: Use -1 where quantity is not applicable. Keep quantmin less than or equal to quantmax.

terms.meaning: Central Economy queue priority; vanilla item entries commonly use 100.
terms.rule: It is not a shop price or currency value.

terms.meaning: Whether copies stored in cargo count toward the economy population.
terms.rule: A value of 1 counts them; 0 ignores that location for this calculation.

terms.meaning: Whether stored/hoarded copies count toward the economy population.
terms.rule: Changing counting flags can materially affect loot availability.

terms.meaning: Whether copies present in the world count toward the economy population.
terms.rule: Normally enabled for world-loot items.

terms.meaning: Whether player-carried copies count toward the economy population.
terms.rule: Use the current vanilla entry as the baseline rather than changing every item alike.

terms.meaning: Flags indicating crafted-only treatment or dynamic-event-loot behaviour in the Central Economy.
terms.rule: Do not set deloot simply to make an item rare; it changes where the economy expects it.

terms.meaning: Distance used to keep an event spawn away from survivors or protected spawning conditions.
terms.rule: Meaning is event-context dependent; compare with the matching vanilla event family.

terms.meaning: Event spacing distance used to prevent eligible events from appearing too close to one another.
terms.rule: It is not the visible radius of the spawned scene.

terms.meaning: Radius used when cleaning event objects around the event position.
terms.rule: A value that is too broad can affect more of the scene than intended.

terms.meaning: Minimum and maximum loot associated with a supported event child or group object.
terms.rule: They do not set the number of child objects; child min/max do that.

terms.meaning: How the event chooses positions, such as fixed, player or uniform.
terms.rule: A fixed event needs suitable entries in cfgeventspawns.xml.

terms.meaning: How event limits are counted, such as child, parent, custom or mixed.
terms.rule: Use the same event family as a vanilla reference before choosing a value.

terms.meaning: Whether the event definition is enabled for the Central Economy.
terms.rule: An active event can still fail when its name, child class or position link is invalid.

terms.meaning: Dynamic minimum and maximum population for an infected or animal territory zone when players activate it.
terms.rule: Large hordes can cause performance problems.

terms.meaning: Static minimum and maximum population for a territory zone.
terms.rule: Static populations can exist independently of normal player-triggered dynamic behaviour.

terms.meaning: World coordinates: X and Z are horizontal map axes; Y is height/elevation where the schema uses it.
terms.rule: Do not swap an iZurvive X/Z pair into a JSON schema expecting X/Y/Z without placing height in the middle.

terms.meaning: Rotation around the vertical axis, normally expressed from 0 to 360 degrees.
terms.rule: Keep enough decimal precision to prevent unwanted rotation changes.

terms.meaning: Radius in metres around a territory or configured point.
terms.rule: It is not a diameter; map boundaries and the feature's own limits still apply.

terms.meaning: Probability for cargo, attachments or preset choices, normally from 0.0 to 1.0.
terms.rule: 1.0 means 100 percent; 0.5 means 50 percent.

terms.meaning: Spawn damage range where 0 is pristine and 1 is ruined.
terms.rule: Keep min less than or equal to max. Ruined items may be unusable or cleaned up.

terms.meaning: Broad loot classification such as weapons, food, tools or clothes.
terms.rule: Custom names must be defined in limits definitions and supported by the related loot chain.

terms.meaning: Location type where loot can be eligible, such as Military, Town, Farm or Hunting.
terms.rule: A types.xml usage must agree with eligible building/group definitions.

terms.meaning: Loot-zone value such as Tier1, Tier2, Tier3 or Tier4.
terms.rule: Map tier zones and bunker tiers are separate concepts; use the correct context.

terms.meaning: economy.xml switches controlling initial creation, persistence loading, respawning and persistence saving for a broad economy group.
terms.rule: 1 enables and 0 disables that behaviour; these switches affect a whole group.

terms.meaning: cfggameplay.json list of relative paths to supported ObjectSpawner JSON files.
terms.rule: The path, filename, extension and letter case must match the uploaded file.

terms.meaning: cfggameplay.json list of supported fresh-spawn loadout preset files.
terms.rule: It does not replace cfgplayerspawnpoints.xml; one controls gear and the other controls location.

terms.meaning: cfggameplay.json list of supported player restricted-area JSON files.
terms.rule: Each referenced file must follow the restricted-area schema, including safe positions.
